title.narrative: Output 2.4. Increased capacity Member States to apply sectoral international labour standards, codes of practice and guidelines

description.narrative:
1. The Government of the Republic of Namibia, through the Ministry Labour, Industrial Relations and Employment Creation’s Labour Services/Inspectorate Department has established a standing National Commission on Decent Work in the Namibian Fisheries Sector adopted from the project’s National Tripartite Advisory Committee in line the principles of the Work in Fishing Convention, 2007(No. 188) and its accompanying Recommendation and flexibility clauses. The action was also informed by the Guidelines on flag State inspection of working and living conditions on board of fishing vessels, 2017 and the Guidelines for port State control officers carrying out inspections under the Work in Fishing Convention, 2007 (No 188), 2010.
a. In 2022, the National Tripartite Advisory Committee developed and adopted an Action Plan to promote decent work and strengthen labour inspection in the fisheries sector b. The first-ever joint labour inspection campaign was successfully implemented by the Ministry of Labour, Industrial Relations and Employment Creation, the Ministry of Fisheries and Marine Resources and the Ministry of Works and Transport, directly benefiting 306 fishermen on board fishing vessels, 294 workers employed by fishing companies and 12 vessel managers. c. A Strategic Compliance Taskforce was created with 12 members from the Government and from workers’ and employers’ organizations to improve coordination among the relevant authorities and to strengthen their ability to apply a strategic compliance planning approach to inspection in the fishing sector. d. Within the framework of strategic compliance planning, the project developed standardized employment contract templates for fishers in the industry that align with national laws and ILO Convention No. 188. Over the period 2022-2023 and with support from the ILO/EU Sustainable Supply Chains to Build Forward Better" project (SSCBFB), in December 2022, the ILO published a Deep-dive research into decent work challenges and opportunities in Namibia’s fishing supply chain. The report highlighted employment trends and working conditions, the challenges to and opportunities for the promotion of decent work. It also outlined recommendations for action by the tripartite partners, as well as investors and other global supply chain players. a. Several capacity building activities were conducted over the period 2022-2023 to improve coordination and to strengthen capacities to apply a strategic compliance planning approach to inspection in the fishing sector. This included a stakeholders’ Sensitization and Training Workshop on the ILO Convention No. 188, basic safety and familiarization training for labour inspectors, and a training programme on occupational safety and health provisions on fishing vessels concluded with certification of 42 labour inspectors, shop stewards, fisheries inspectors, and fisheries observers from the harbour of Walvis Bay and Lüderitz. b. Several tools have been developed to support the work of inspectors in the fishing sector including A Toolkit that contains a Namibia Field Guide on Labour Inspection On Board Fishing Vessels and two leaflets, on “Basic Employment Conditions for Decent Work” and ‘’How to Stay Safe While Working On a Fishing Vessel At Sea”. c. National inspectors were trained on the use of these materials to improve conditions in the industry. c. A sensitization workshop on convention No.190 was conducted to raise awareness and address violence and harassment in the fishing sector. d. A stakeholder engagement on the variation of Chapter 3 of the Labour Act for the fisheries sector was conducted and it aimed raising awareness of the recently gazetted variation No.38 of 2023.

description.narrative: 1. The Government of the Republic of Namibia has strengthened sectoral mechanisms for collective bargaining and workplace cooperation in the fishing, security, construction, retail and mining sectors : a. Thirty(30) negotiators in the sectors have enhanced their capacity and knowledge on wage setting that has resulted in the signing of collective bargaining agreements and the setting of the first sectoral minimum wage in the fishing sector. b. 28 Workers and Employers representatives in the fishing sector were trained on collective bargaining in pilot of the IRToolkit and in particular of the new module on Freedom of Association. 1. In September 2023, through the ILO/EU Sustainable Supply Chains to Build Forward Better" project (SSCBFB) project, negotiators from employers and workers in the fishing were trained on negotiation skills for effective collective bargaining. The training programme drew from training materials designed by the ILO and the ITC/ILO including the IRToolkit ( module on freedom of association) that have been successfully used in various countries. A second training workshop was conducted in October 2023, for negotiators from the security, construction, retail and mining sectors with support from Regular Budget Technical Cooperation(RBTC) support.

description.narrative: 1. The Ministry of Labour Industrial Relations and Employment Creation through its Office of the Labour Commissioner (OLC) has strengthened its arbitration and conciliation capacities for dispute prevention and resolution to reduce its case backlog and address comments of the ILO Supervisory Bodies on the application in law and practice of the Convention on Discrimination (Employment and Occupation) Convention, 1958 (No. 111): a. The capacities developed and strengthened include drafting of settlement awards in conciliation and of awards in arbitration cases and specific orientation to adjudication of cases related to discrimination (C100 & C111) in the world of work including violence and harassment(C190). b. From the year April 2021 to March 2022 to April 2022 to March 2023 the case backlog has been reduced by 360 cases equivalent to about 23% of the case load. The Office has supported the Ministry of Labour Industrial Relations and Employment Creation, and its Office of the Labour Commissioner (OLC), providing the necessary assistance, for example capacity building of the staff, to take into account comments of the ILO Supervisory Bodies on the application in law and practice of the Convention on Discrimination (Employment and Occupation) Convention, 1958 (No. 111). The result of this support is that the case backlog has been reduced by 23% in the last two years.
